commentary: Sweden's GDP growth of 0.82% in 2024 — following a -0.2% contraction in 2023 — provides the economic context for the government's migration enforcement tightening via SfU22: fiscal pressure on welfare costs incentivizes reducing the population of individuals in enforcement limbo. At the same time, Sweden's $603.7B GDP creates capacity to invest in the state e-ID infrastructure (TU21) required for eIDAS2 EU compliance, while the agricultural sector's contribution to Sweden's economic base underlines why MJU21's climate conditions remain politically sensitive for rural constituencies.
